p01.why: Each declarator's initializer is its own full expression, so T{1} ends before T{2} is made, giving 1, 9, 2, 9.

p02.why: The condition is a full expression, so the temporary ends (9) before the branch runs mark(1), giving 91.

p03.why: val() is a prvalue of type int, and a non-class prvalue cannot be assigned to.

p04.why: The discarded class prvalue becomes a temporary that ends at the end of its statement, so 1 is logged before 9.

p05.why: A reference member of a prvalue gives an lvalue, so int& binds to g; there is no main to run.

p06.why: Subscripting the array prvalue makes a temporary array, and element 1 is 2, so main returns 0.

p07.why: .* on an xvalue for a data member gives an xvalue, so decltype gives int&&.

p08.why: The default-argument temporary lives until the end of the full expression with the call, giving 1, 9, 2.

p09.why: A class prvalue can be assigned to, because assignment is a member function call; no main.

p10.why: Each prvalue initializes its target directly, so S() runs once for a and once for b, and made is 2.

p11.why: A cast to an rvalue reference to a function type gives an lvalue, so its address can be taken.

p12.why: A subscript of an array xvalue or array prvalue is an xvalue, so both give int&& (EDG reportedly differs, Q-0099).

p13.why: .* on the class prvalue makes a temporary that ends at the end of the declaration, so x is 7 and the order is 1, 2.

p14.why: f() is a prvalue of non-class type, which has no cv-qualifiers, so decltype gives int.

p15.why: Member access on the class prvalue makes a temporary whose v is 7.

p16.why: get runs (1), the temporary ends at the end of the declaration (2), then mark(3), giving 123.

p17.why: Each operand is a prvalue, so decltype gives the plain type in each case.

p18.why: The discarded class prvalue makes a temporary, which needs a usable destructor, and D's destructor is deleted.

p19.why: All initializers of one aggregate are one full expression, so both temporaries end after both reads, giving 1, 2, 9, 9.

p20.why: Constant evaluation materializes both temporaries as at run time and gets 3 + 4 = 7; no main.

p21.why: A member access that names a non-static member function can only be called, so its address cannot be taken.

p22.why: r binds to a temporary and m binds to a member of one, and both temporaries live as long as the references, so both read 3.

p23.why: this, the enumerator, the cast to long, and (x, 0) are prvalues; the cast to int& and (0, x) are lvalues; all asserts match.

p24.why: The parameter ends either at the return of take (192) or at the end of the full expression (129), and the program accepts both.

p25.why: The name of an rvalue reference variable is an lvalue, so decltype((r)) is int&.

p26.why: A program must not take the address of a prvalue.

p27.why: The prvalues initialize a and b directly, so the deleted copy and move constructors are never needed.

p28.why: In decltype, a call makes no temporary, so the deleted destructor is not needed.

p29.why: The temporary passed through pass lives to the end of the full expression, so read sees 5, then 9, then 2.

p30.why: The return expression's temporary ends before the local, giving 1, 2, 3.

p31.why: A cast to int&&, a call returning int&&, and a member of an xvalue or class prvalue are all xvalues, so each gives int&&.

p32.why: A data member of an lvalue, by . or ->, is an lvalue, so decltype gives int& and the addresses can be taken.

p33.why: The array prvalue becomes a temporary when it converts to a pointer, and it lives through the call, so the sum is 1 + 3 = 4.

p34.why: Both temporaries live until the end of the full expression, so seen is 0, both are logged in one of the two orders, then 9.

p35.why: A cast to an rvalue reference to an object type is an xvalue, and a program must not take the address of an xvalue.

p36.why: Each operand is an lvalue, and a string literal is an lvalue array of 3 const char, so each decltype is a reference type as written.

p37.why: Whether the parameter shares the caller's address is unspecified, but the program returns 0 either way.

p38.why: make() is a prvalue of type int, which cannot be assigned to.

p39.why: A static data member accessed through a prvalue gives an lvalue, so its address can be taken; no main, so the missing make does not matter.

p40.why: Each element's default-argument temporary ends before the next element is built, giving 1, 9, 1, 9.

p41.why: r is an lvalue of type int, and an rvalue reference must not bind to an lvalue of the same type.
